messages:
Jess: heads-up — after landing the `cuda-toolkit:12.1` base image for inference containers, ~10% of pods in the dedicated-gpu-pool are CrashLoopBackOffing on startup :grimacing:
Mike: logs? error codes?
Jess: paste of pod logs:
```
/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.29' not found
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc: failed call to cuInit: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN: unknown error
NCCL WARN Call to cuDeviceGet returned error 999
```
Santiago: that nvcc/glibc mismatch screams container rebuilt against newer toolchain (gcc/libstdc++) — we bumped base image and also switched to `gcc-12` in the Dockerfile last week.
Jess: right. we also see `driver API mismatch` in some nodes when running `nvidia-smi`:
```
NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver. Driver Version: 525.60.13  CUDA Version: 11.8
```
but containers expect runtime symbols from CUDA 12.x (fatbins from nvcc12).
OpsBot: [ALERT] 2025-11-12T10:34:20Z metric: gpu.pod_start_failures up 73% in us-west2-dedicated (svc=inference-serving)
Eva: is this region-specific? eu-west1 had no issues yesterday.
Ryan: eu-west1 hosts are still on driver 535.x patched by kernel update earlier — us-west2 nodes are stuck on 525.x because the kernel rollout failed during last maintenance. so mixed fleet state.
Mike: so we have two simultaneous compatibility problems: container/libstdc++ ABI mismatch AND driver/CUDA runtime mismatch. That explains why some pods crash immediately and others behave fine (depending on host driver).
Santiago: bonus fun: NCCL 2.18 compiled with CUDA12 uses new PTX sm versions; older driver fails with weird segfaults during allreduce init.
Jess: quick mitigation proposed: revert inference base image to pinned `cuda-toolkit:11.8` tag and rollout tonight, then schedule driver upgrades + kernel modules in a controlled window.
Eva: agree. we should also add a preflight probe in the CI that runs `nvidia-smi`, `cuInit()` smoke, and a small NCCL ring launch against a staging GPU node before publishing images.
Ryan: operational constraints: draining 40 nodes in dedicated-gpu-pool will drop capacity by ~30% for 3 hours. if we revert images we can avoid immediate drain, but we need drivers upgraded within 7 days or the divergence reappears.
Jess: cost impact: we already had to spin up 8 ephemeral GPU instances to keep SLAs (on-demand), estimate ~$1800/day extra if prolonged. tagging ticket #OPS-789 for cost tracking.
Mike: low-effort hotfix: in the Dockerfile rebuild, we can unpack NVCC fatbins with `-arch` fallback flags to produce compatibility with older drivers, but that's messy and still fragile. prefer pin + patch driver.
Santiago: also note kernel module ABI: some hosts still run custom tuned kernels (security vendor) that block driver 535 installs without vendor package. need coordination with partners team.
Deploy-Bot: deploy rolldown detected: 1759498000 - image inference/base:cuda-12.1 pushed -> 120 containers updated across clusters.
Jess: timeline proposal:
  1) immediate: tag and push rollback image inference/base:cuda-11.8-pinned, update k8s daemonset to use that tag for dedicated pools (hotfix) — ETA 30m
  2) tonight: CI image gating + NCCL smoke tests in staging (2h)
  3) Wed 02:00 UTC: scheduled driver rollout in us-west2 with kernel package prechecks; drain 10 nodes at a time, canaries first (4h maintenance window)
  4) post-mortem & add a preflight matrix: {image cuda-toolkit, host-driver, kernel-version} to release checklist
Eva: can QA validate that rolling back to cuda-11 doesn't regress performance for existing models? we should run a quick perf sample on a few heavy routes.
Ryan: we'll run a 30-min perf sweep on a canary set; if we see >5% latency regression, we open emergency meeting.
Mike: logging checklist for next release: capture `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version,name --format=csv`, `ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/libcuda.so`, and `gcc -v` during image build.
Jess: assigning owners: Jess -> push rollback, Mike -> CI smoke tests, Santiago -> driver rollout playbook updates, Eva -> perf validation, Ryan -> capacity/maintenance coordination.
OpsBot: [NOTE] INC-4321 created to track rollback and driver upgrade scheduling.
Santiago: long term: lock our release matrix so toolchain major upgrades require a staged infra upgrade (driver+kernel) before image promotion.
Eva: also propose an automated compatibility matrix dashboard in Console showing host driver vs image runtime compatibility per region.
Jess: thanks everyone. I'll publish the rollback PR and tag the ops on-call. :thumbsup:
Ryan: ping me if you need help draining nodes, I'm on-call today. :eyes:
Deploy-Bot: rollback job started 1759501410 -> updating 120 pods across clusters
Jess: will post updates here as each step completes.
